data.narrative:
Spiritus is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Charles Cadieu and Matthew Lee that has raised $41M to date. The broader sector comprises one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix. However, no narrow peer set of same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables with sufficient data density exists to support a reliable peer-median valuation method.

The stage-progression method applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage transitions, using total capital raised as a valuation proxy. This yields an implied valuation of $82M. The peer-median approach is not applicable due to insufficient datapoints in filtered peer cohorts; applying all-sector medians would introduce material bias given the heterogeneity within Climate & Energy stage and business model distribution.

The analysis triangulates to a range of $70M (low) to $94M (high), with a median of $82M, derived from a single method. Key uncertainties center on the applicability of a 2.0x multiplier to this specific company and stage, the absence of direct comparables to calibrate either growth or risk profiles, and the reliance on capital raised rather than independent revenue or margin metrics. Additional market data on recent Series A and Series B closings in frontier climate tech would substantially narrow this range.
